title: The Batch
subtitle: Save it. Revisit it. Make it count.
description: A phone-friendly weekly feed that brings starred Gmail and X bookmarks into one place, with item state and discussion threads that carry over from week to week.
capabilities: Saturday refresh through GitHub Actions
Persistent new, seen, sparred, acted, and dismissed states
Portable JSON context store shared by the feed and a desktop client
note: Write-back is asynchronous: browser changes are exported manually and folded into the next scheduled batch. No private saved items are reproduced here.
problem: Saved links are easy to collect and hard to return to. A weekly feed makes revisiting them intentional instead of another endless inbox.
how: A scheduled GitHub Actions job builds a static feed from a JSON context store. Phone changes are queued locally and exported manually; the next batch folds them back into the store.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The published artifact connects a static phone-friendly feed, a portable context store, and an asynchronous write-back workflow. Private saved items and account configuration are not part of this portfolio.

title: Lineage
subtitle: Give your conversations room to branch.
description: A local-first workspace that turns GitHub Copilot CLI conversations into a branching knowledge tree. Explore a new direction without losing where an idea came from.
capabilities: Branch from addressable Markdown blocks
Keep parent context without leaking sibling conversations
Own an inspectable, Git-backed vault of Markdown and metadata
note: The application runs on localhost. The project site is a walkthrough, not a hosted multi-user app.
imageAlt: Lineage application showing a conversation alongside its branching knowledge tree
problem: A linear agent conversation makes it hard to try another direction without losing the source of an idea or dragging in unrelated branches.
how: FastAPI serves a React interface on localhost. Copilot CLI responses become addressable Markdown blocks; a new branch carries its root-to-fork lineage but excludes sibling branches. Git-backed files keep the tree inspectable.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public project combines a branching conversation interface with an inspectable Markdown-and-metadata knowledge model. Copilot CLI supplies the underlying agent capability; the walkthrough is not a hosted multi-user service.

title: After the meeting
subtitle: Less transcript digging. More answers.
description: A Microsoft Teams sample that retrieves meeting transcripts through Microsoft Graph and answers post-meeting questions with speaker- and timestamp-aware citations.
capabilities: Handle Teams meeting and participant events
Retrieve transcripts through Microsoft Graph
Answer transcript questions with speaker and timestamp citations
note: Preview, not production-ready. Transcript jobs and documents use JSON files on one App Service instance. Distributed leases, legal hold, user deletion, and multi-instance consistency remain production gaps. Use non-sensitive test meetings only.
problem: Finding a specific answer in a completed meeting should not require manually searching an entire transcript.
how: Teams meeting events trigger transcript retrieval through Graph. The .NET sample uses Microsoft Agent Framework and Azure OpenAI to answer questions from the retrieved transcript with citations.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. This is an adaptation of a Microsoft Teams sample with a documented transcript-question-answering workflow and deployment configuration. Microsoft services and the original sample are dependencies, not original components claimed by this portfolio.

title: Modding, with guardrails
subtitle: A better co-op partner for Minecraft tools.
description: An agent skill for working safely inside MCreator: editing procedures, coordinating Blockly and generated Java, and tracing what happens in a live Minecraft session.
capabilities: Regeneration-aware workspace editing guidance
Blockly procedure and Java coordination
Real-time Minecraft log tracing with PowerShell helpers
note: Not an official MCreator automation API. The skill documents where regeneration can overwrite external edits.
problem: An edit can compile yet disappear when MCreator regenerates Java, or never reach the running game. Several representations need to stay consistent.
how: The skill guides agents through workspace inspection, closing the editor, coordinating Blockly and generated Java, compilation, and real-time Minecraft tracing. Runtime state must be verified separately from compilation.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public toolkit packages a safety-focused agent skill, PowerShell inspection helpers, a user quick start, and a documented right-click conversion example. It is an independent field guide, not an official MCreator API.

title: Grand Reset
subtitle: A little space to see the bigger picture.
description: A calm, local-first canvas for mapping a physical and digital declutter. Switch perspectives, organize the loose ends, and review agent proposals before accepting them.
capabilities: Canvas, grid, and flow views
Search, filter, and edit across lifecycle spaces
Browser-local snapshots and an agent proposal inbox
note: There is no remote backend. Saved state belongs to the browser origin rather than a synced account.
problem: Physical and digital loose ends can feel like one undifferentiated pile. Seeing them spatially can offer perspective without turning them into a deadline-driven task list.
how: A static browser application stores the canonical snapshot in localStorage. Canvas, Grid, and Flow are views of the same data. Agent proposals enter a visible inbox and require human approval.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public application explores a local-first life-map model, multiple views, and an explicit human-review boundary for agent proposals. No personal canvas contents are reproduced here.

title: Just Play
subtitle: One good choice. Then settle in.
description: A gaming companion that helps you find up to three games from a curated catalog to fit your mood, energy, and time, then keep the session in view with StandBy.
capabilities: Mood, energy, and time produce a shortlist of up to three games
Session goals and notes help you pick up where you left off
StandBy shows game art, a timer, and session controls
note: V2 is in progress. The public landing and reel are available; an authenticated player workflow was not tested for this portfolio. Steam library sync and launching games are not promised. Canopy relationships and account-backed world growth remain future work.
problem: A large backlog can turn a free evening into more scrolling. The aim is to make a small deliberate choice and keep the game, not the companion, at the center.
how: The public landing describes a curated-catalog recommendation flow and a quiet StandBy companion. The repository uses Next.js, Supabase, and IGDB; its staged public screenshots are demos, not evidence of live account behavior.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public project brings together a game-discovery flow, a StandBy session companion, and a public landing with a silent-first product reel. The source distinguishes implemented foundations from future Canopy direction.

title: RepoQuest
subtitle: Every repository has an opening scene.
description: A TypeScript CLI that turns a GitHub repository into a cinematic setup guide: from README and package details to an animated, self-contained HTML tutorial.
capabilities: Read repository setup signals and environment examples
Generate a ten-scene animated HTML guide
Support video rendering through HyperFrames
note: Produces a tutorial artifact, not a running copy of the source application. Available as npx repoquest.
imageAlt: RepoQuest cinematic repository setup guide example
problem: A repository can have good setup information and still feel hard to begin. A short visual walkthrough can make the opening steps more approachable.
how: The TypeScript CLI reads setup signals from repository files and produces a self-contained HTML guide. Optional HyperFrames support renders a video; generating a guide does not install or run the source project.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public CLI packages repository inspection and an animated tutorial output format. Its example capture is public project imagery; this overview does not repeat the README’s unverified production-grade or accessibility certification claims. The README references upstream qwibitai/repoquest; the available evidence does not resolve Jorge’s individual contribution or authorship.

Memory exercises and reflection prompts
A deliberately small collection of essential insights

how: The public onboarding introduces ephemeral notes, memory exercises, and essential insights. This portfolio describes that public surface only; it does not infer a storage architecture or a validated cognitive outcome.

title: A token stays with the broker
subtitle: An agent can use a tool without holding the user’s token.
description: A proof of concept that puts OAuth credential handling in Azure API Management so a Foundry agent can call a narrow Microsoft Graph tool without receiving the user’s access token.
capabilities: APIM validates a managed-identity caller before tool use
Credential Manager owns the consent, token cache, and refresh
A public explainer and template document the bounded integration
note: The README reports runtime and negative-path checks for one bounded approach. Per-user isolation / per-user OAuth passthrough is not proven. This portfolio did not redeploy the infrastructure or independently repeat those provider checks. No tenant screenshots or identifiers are reproduced.
problem: Giving an agent a user’s token expands the consequences of a leak. A narrow broker can keep the credential boundary separate from the model.
how: The Foundry agent authenticates to APIM with a managed identity. APIM validates the caller, obtains a token from Credential Manager, calls Graph, and returns the tool result rather than the credential.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public artifact includes an architectural walkthrough, an interactive diagram, APIM integration work, and a reusable Bicep template. It documents both the chosen approach and the limits of what its reported checks establish.
